sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: MID-UPPER LEVEL PATTERN WILL CONTINUE TO FEATURE ZONALLY ELONGATED ANTICYCLONE OVER SRN PLAINS...AND PROGRESSIVE/HIGH-AMPLITUDE SHORTWAVE TROUGH MOVING FROM NRN PLAINS EWD ACROSS UPPER MS VALLEY AND UPPER GREAT LAKES. LATTER PERTURBATION AT 500 MB CURRENTLY EXTENDS FROM SRN PORTIONS MB/SK BORDER REGION SWWD ACROSS SWRN WY...AND SHOULD REACH FROM NRN MN TO S-CENTRAL NEB BY 5/00Z. NEAR END OF PERIOD...TROUGH SHOULD BE LOCATED FROM NWRN ONT ACROSS LS...NRN WI...ERN IA...AND NRN MO. ASSOCIATED SFC COLD FRONT -- MOVING EWD ACROSS UPPER MS VALLEY AND SEWD OVER NEB ATTM -- SHOULD REACH ERN WI...NERN MO...SERN KS AND TX PANHANDLE BY 5/00Z. FRONT SHOULD EXTEND FROM LH TO SERN IL...SERN MO...SERN OK...AND SERN NM BY END OF PERIOD. DURING LATE AFTERNOON...WEAK/RESIDUAL FRONTAL ZONE WILL LINGER FROM SERN KS SEWD OVER MID-SOUTH REGION...DEMARCATING NERN RIM OF HOT/WELL-MIXED BOUNDARY LAYER OF SRN PLAINS. THIS BOUNDARY WILL BE OVERTAKEN FROM W-E BY COLD FRONT. LOW-LEVEL FRONTAL ZONE NOW OVER NRN PORTIONS NY/NEW ENGLAND SHOULD MOVE SLOWLY NEWD TODAY.

sections.title: UPPER GREAT LAKES TO MO AND LOWER OH VALLEY
sections.text: SCATTERED-NUMEROUS TSTMS SHOULD FORM ALONG/AHEAD OF COLD FRONT BETWEEN NRN MO AND UPPER MI DURING AFTERNOON...POSING PRIMARY RISK OF WIND DAMAGE WITH SECONDARY HAIL THREAT. CONVECTION CURRENTLY CROSSING UPPER MS VALLEY REGION AHEAD OF SFC COLD FRONT IS SOMEWHAT AHEAD OF 00Z MODEL GUIDANCE...INDICATING MORE EWD POSITION OF RESIDUAL CLOUD/PRECIP SHIELD BY START OF PERIOD OVER WI AND IA. NARROW CORRIDOR OF ADVECTIVELY AND DIABATICALLY DRIVEN RECOVERY MAY OCCUR BETWEEN BACK SIDE OF THIS PLUME AND SFC COLD FRONT DURING DAY. HOWEVER...MORE PROBABLE SCENARIO INVOLVES RE-INTENSIFICATION OF THIS ACTIVITY OR NEW DEVELOPMENT OF TSTMS ALONG ITS BOUNDARY FROM LATE MORNING/EARLY AFTERNOON ONWARD. THIS SHOULD OCCUR AS STG DIABATIC HEATING AND FAVORABLE MOISTURE IN PRECONVECTIVE BOUNDARY LAYER WEAKEN CINH. FARTHER SW ACROSS IA INTO NRN MO/NERN KS...THERE WILL BE LESS INFLUENCE AND SPATIAL UNCERTAINTY RESULTING FROM EARLY-PERIOD ACTIVITY. CONFIDENCE IS STG IN COLD FRONT BEING PRIMARY TSTM INITIATOR...THOUGH WARM-SECTOR TSTMS MAY FORM OVER PORTIONS NRN MO AND IL DURING AFTERNOON AS WELL. SFC DEW POINTS MID-60S TO LOW-70S F...OVER MUCH OF PRECONVECTIVE WARM SECTOR FROM NRN MO TO WRN SHORE OF LM WILL

sections.title: NERN CONUS
sections.text: SCATTERED TSTMS SHOULD DEVELOP NEAR AND SW OF FRONTAL ZONE DURING AFTERNOON...AS WARM/MOIST ADVECTION COMBINE WITH SFC DIABATIC HEATING TO REDUCE CINH. RICH LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE -- I.E. 1.5-1.75 INCH PW AND SFC DEW POINTS MID-60S TO LOW-70S F -- WILL SUPPORT MLCAPE AROUND 2000 J/KG. ORGANIZATION OF THIS ACTIVITY WILL BE LIMITED BY LACK OF SUBSTANTIAL MID-UPPER SUPPORT...AND WEAK DEEP-LAYER FLOW...BUT A FEW STG-SVR GUSTS AND MRGL HAIL REPORTS ARE POSSIBLE.

sections.title: SERN CONUS
sections.text: SCATTERED TO LOCALLY NUMEROUS MULTICELLULAR TSTMS IN CLUSTERS SHOULD DEVELOP OVER BROAD SWATH FROM TN VALLEY TO CENTRAL GULF COAST REGION...INVOF WEAK AXIS OF MID-UPPER LEVEL VORTICITY...AS STG INSOLATION AND RICH BOUNDARY-LAYER MOISTURE REMOVE MLCINH. SOME POTENTIAL EXISTS FOR AGGREGATE COLD-POOL GROWTH FROM MULTICELLULAR CLUSTERS...HOWEVER THIS RISK WILL BE DRIVEN STRONGLY BY STORM-SCALE TO MESOBETA SCALE PROCESSES OF UNCERTAIN TIMING/PLACEMENT. ..EDWARDS/GARNER.. 08/04/2012

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: UPPER SHORT WAVE TROUGH MOVING ACROSS THE NRN PLAINS IS FORECAST TO GRADUALLY DEEPEN AS IT MOVES EWD...REACHING THE UPPER MS VALLEY BY THE END OF THE PERIOD. AT THE SURFACE...PRIMARY LOW OVER NWRN ONTARIO WILL MOVE NEWD TOWARD JAMES BAY...AS A COLD FRONT CURRENTLY TRAILING SWD FROM THE LOW ACROSS MN AND WRN IA THEN SWWD ACROSS THE CENTRAL PLAINS MOVES EWD/SEWD...REACHING A LOWER MI/SRN IL/CENTRAL OK/NWRN TX LINE LATE TONIGHT. AS THIS FRONT MOVES SEWD IT WILL MERGE WITH AND OVERTAKE A QUASI-STATIONARY FRONT EXTENDING FROM THE TX PANHANDLE INTO ERN KS/SRN IL AND NRN KY.

sections.title: GREAT LAKES INTO THE LOWER MO RIVER VALLEY
sections.text: A PRE-FRONTAL LINE OF NOCTURNAL CONVECTION ARCING FROM UPPER MI ACROSS WI INTO NRN IA HAS WEAKENED CONSIDERABLY DURING THE PRE-DAWN HOURS...ALTHOUGH AN EXTENSIVE AREA OF CLOUDS AND WIDELY SCATTERED CONVECTION IS EVIDENT ACROSS THIS REGION. IN ADDITION...ELEVATED STORMS CONTINUE FROM CENTRAL MO INTO SRN IL ALONG THE NWRN FLANK OF A SWLY LOW LEVEL JET AND ASSOCIATED WARM ADVECTION REGION. THE CONVECTION IS GENERALLY EXPECTED TO WEAKEN FURTHER THIS MORNING...ALTHOUGH REMNANT OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES MAY PERSIST AND SERVE AS A FOCUS FOR SUBSEQUENT THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT THIS AFTERNOON. AS SOUTHERLY LOW LEVEL WINDS BECOME BETTER ESTABLISHED AHEAD OF THE APPROACHING COLD FRONT AND/OR OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES...MOISTURE WILL INCREASE NWD WITH SURFACE DEW POINTS IN THE UPPER 60S TO LOWER 70S THIS AFTERNOON. STRONGER DIABATIC HEATING AND DESTABILIZATION IS EXPECTED OVER PARTS OF SRN WI...ERN IA AND NRN IL WHERE FEWER CLOUDS ARE NOTED IN MORNING SATELLITE IMAGERY WHICH WILL RESULT IN MLCAPE REACHING 2000-3500 J/KG THIS AFTERNOON. WEAK LOW LEVEL CONVERGENCE ALONG BOUNDARIES AND THE COLD FRONT COUPLED WITH HEATING WILL REDUCE THE CIN SUFFICIENTLY BY EARLY AFTERNOON FOR NEW STORMS TO DEVELOP FROM PARTS O

sections.title: PA/NY INTO WRN NEW ENGLAND
sections.text: WIDELY SCATTERED TSTMS SHOULD DEVELOP NEAR AND SW OF A WEAKENING FRONTAL ZONE DURING THE AFTERNOON...AS WARM/MOIST ADVECTION COMBINE WITH SURFACE DIABATIC HEATING TO REDUCE CINH. SURFACE DEW POINTS IN THE MID 60S AND AMPLE DIURNAL HEATING WILL CONTRIBUTE TO STRONG DESTABILIZATION WITH MLCAPE REACHING 1500-2500 J/KG. THIS WILL SUPPORT VIGOROUS CONVECTIVE UPDRAFTS BUT ORGANIZATION OF THIS ACTIVITY WILL BE LIMITED BY WEAK WINDS ALOFT AND MINIMAL VERTICAL SHEAR. ISOLATED STORMS MAY PRODUCE STRONG WIND GUSTS AND HAIL THIS AFTERNOON. ..WEISS/SMITH.. 08/04/2012

sections.title: UPPER GREAT LAKES/MID MS VALLEY/SRN PLAINS THROUGH TONIGHT
sections.text: A PRONOUNCED SHORTWAVE TROUGH WILL PROGRESS EWD/ESEWD FROM THE DAKOTAS/NW MN TO THE UPPER MS VALLEY BY THIS EVENING/OVERNIGHT. THE MIDLEVEL TROUGH WILL BE PRECEDED BY A SURFACE COLD FRONT WHICH IS NOW MOVING EWD FROM ERN MN TO WRN WI...AND SEWD ACROSS CENTRAL IA/NW MO/ERN KS. THE IMPACTS OF OVERNIGHT CONVECTION HAVE COMPLICATED THE SURFACE PATTERN WITH A REMNANT OUTFLOW BOUNDARY ARCING SWWD FROM ERN WI ACROSS NW IL TO SE IA. THE STRONGEST SURFACE HEATING IS ONGOING S OF THE OUTFLOW BOUNDARY ACROSS SE IA AND IL...WHERE THE RICHEST BOUNDARY LAYER MOISTURE /DEWPOINTS IN THE LOW 70S/ IS PRESENT. FARTHER S/SW...A SEPARATE BAND OF CLOUDS AND SOME EMBEDDED CONVECTION COVERS NRN/ERN MO AND SRN IL IN ASSOCIATION WITH LOW-LEVEL WAA NEAR AND W OF THE MS RIVER...AND A SECONDARY SURFACE LOW IN NRN MO. CONVECTION HAS ALREADY BEEN INCREASING SINCE MID MORNING ALONG THE COLD FRONT IN CENTRAL IA...AND IN ASSOCIATION WITH A SEPARATE EMBEDDED SPEED MAX ALOFT IN ADVANCE OF THE PRIMARY MIDLEVEL TROUGH. IT APPEARS THE IA STORMS WILL CONTINUE TO SPREAD EWD INTO THE REGION OF STRONGEST SURFACE HEATING/BUOYANCY ACROSS SE IA AND NRN IL THROUGH THE AFTERNOON. EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR WILL INCREASE TO ROUGHLY 35-

sections.title: APPALACHIANS TO NEW ENGLAND THIS AFTERNOON
sections.text: WEAK FLOW ALOFT AND NO OBVIOUS SURFACE BOUNDARIES SUGGEST THAT TERRAIN INFLUENCES AND DAYTIME HEATING WILL BE THE PRIMARY IMPETUS FOR STORM DEVELOPMENT THIS AFTERNOON. MODERATE BUOYANCY/LAPSE RATES...PER MODIFIED 12Z SOUNDINGS...SUPPORT A MARGINAL RISK FOR DAMAGING WINDS/HAIL. ..THOMPSON/MOSIER.. 08/04/2012

sections.title: NRN IL...SRN WI...NRN IN
sections.text: AN MCS CONTINUES TO TREK EWD ACROSS NRN IL...AND WILL ENTER FAR SERN WI AND PERHAPS NRN IND LATER THIS AFTERNOON. DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE THE PRIMARY THREAT WITH THIS ORGANIZED COMPLEX...WHICH MAY PERSIST DURING THE EVENING INTO WRN OH.

sections.title: SWRN MO INTO SERN KS...NRN AND WRN OK...TX PANHANDLE
sections.text: VISIBLE IMAGERY SHOWS RAPID CU GROWTH ALONG THE COLD FRONT FROM THE TX PANHANDLE NEWD ACROSS NRN OK. CONTINUED HEATING AS WELL AS CONVERGENCE SHOULD RESULT IN ISOLATED THUNDERSTORMS WHICH WILL BE HIGH BASED WITH INDIVIDUAL CELLS SHORT LIVED. HOWEVER...SOME PROPAGATION MAY OCCUR AS OUTFLOWS SURGE...WITH THE PRIMARY THREAT BEING DAMAGING OUTFLOW WINDS. HAVE SHIFTED THE 5 PERCENT WIND PROBABILITIES FARTHER S TO ACCOUNT FOR CURRENT BOUNDARY POSITION. FARTHER NE INTO KS AND MO...A PLUME OF HOT TEMPERATURES CONTINUES TO EXPAND NEWD TOWARDS THE COLD FRONT. RAPID THUNDERSTORM DEVELOP IS EXPECTED ACROSS CNTRL MO AND SERN KS...WHERE INSTABILITY AND FLOW ALOFT ARE STRONGER. DAMAGING WINDS AND SOME HAIL WILL BE LIKELY WITH THESE STORMS...WHICH MAY PROPAGATE SEWD TOWARDS FAR WRN KY WHERE THE SLIGHT AS BEEN EXPANDED. ..JEWELL.. 08/04/2012 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1130 AM CDT SAT AUG 04 2012/

sections.title: APPALACHIANS TO NEW ENGLAND THIS AFTERNOON
sections.text: WEAK FLOW ALOFT AND NO OBVIOUS SURFACE BOUNDARIES SUGGEST THAT TERRAIN INFLUENCES AND DAYTIME HEATING WILL BE THE PRIMARY IMPETUS FOR STORM DEVELOPMENT THIS AFTERNOON. MODERATE BUOYANCY/LAPSE RATES...PER MODIFIED 12Z SOUNDINGS...SUPPORT A MARGINAL RISK FOR DAMAGING WINDS/HAIL.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A CONTINUED INCREASE IN TSTM COVERAGE AND INTENSITY IS EXPECTED INTO THE AFTERNOON HOURS. SVR TSTMS WITH A THREAT FOR DAMAGING WINDS AND PERHAPS LARGE HAIL ARE EXPECTED. A WW WILL LIKELY BE NEEDED FOR PORTIONS OF THIS AREA BY 16Z-17Z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: TSTMS CONTINUE TO INCREASE IN COVERAGE IN ADVANCE OF A COLD FRONT EXTENDING FROM ERN MN SWD THROUGH CENTRAL IA/NWRN MO. A QUASI-STNRY FRONT ACROSS NRN MO IS ALSO HELPING TO FOCUS LOW-LEVEL CONVERGENCE. OBJECTIVE ANALYSIS INDICATES THE ATMOSPHERE IN ADVANCE OF THE AREA OF CONVECTION CONTINUES TO DESTABILIZE WITH DIURNAL HEATING...WITH MLCAPE VALUES CURRENTLY 1000-2000 J/KG. STRONGER FLOW ALOFT IS RESULTING IN EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR VALUES OF 40-50 KT...SUFFICIENT FOR MULTICELL STORM ORGANIZATION WITH SOME SUPERCELL STRUCTURES POSSIBLE. AS FURTHER DESTABILIZATION OCCURS...THE PRIMARY THREATS WILL BE DAMAGING WINDS...ALTHOUGH LARGE HAIL IS POSSIBLE WITH ANY SUPERCELLS THAT DEVELOP. A GRADUAL INCREASE IN COVERAGE IS EXPECTED THROUGH EARLY AFTERNOON AS A SEASONABLY STRONG UPPER LEVEL TROUGH OVER THE CENTRAL/NRN PLAINS MOVES EWD PROVIDING ADDITIONAL FORCING FOR ASCENT. WATER VAPOR LOOPS ALSO SUGGEST A WEAKER DISTURBANCE EMBEDDED WITHIN MONSOONAL FLOW ON THE NRN PERIPHERY OF MID-LEVEL ANTICYCLONE WILL ALSO PROVIDE ADDITIONAL FORCING.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A LINE OF TSTMS WILL CONTINUE PROGRESSING EWD ACROSS SERN IA INTO NRN IL. PRIMARY SEVERE THREAT OF DAMAGING WINDS WITH THE LOW PROBABILITY OF A FEW SEVERE HAIL REPORTS WILL EXIST AS LINE CONTINUES EWD. A DOWNSTREAM WW WILL LIKELY BE NEEDED WITHIN THE NEXT HOUR OR TWO.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: RECENT DVN RADAR TRENDS HAVE SHOWN IMPROVED CONVECTIVE STRUCTURE WITH INCREASED ORGANIZATION OVER THE PAST HOUR. DVN BASE VELOCITY DATA HAS ALSO SHOWN AN INCREASING TREND WITH MAX WINDS LOCATED ACROSS CEDAR COUNTY IA. ADDITIONALLY...RECENT SURFACE OBSERVATIONS DEPICT A WELL-DEFINED RISE-FALL-RISE PRESSURE TREND ALONG AND JUST BEHIND THE LINE...FURTHER VERIFYING THE STRENGTH/MATURITY OF THE MCS. MLCAPE AOA 2000 J/KG...SUPPORTED BY MOSTLY CLEAR SKIES...TEMPERATURES IN THE UPPER 80S/LOW 90S...AND DEWPOINT VALUES IN THE UPPER 60S/LOW 70S...EXISTS DOWNSTREAM OF THE LINE. LATEST MESOANALYSIS ALSO SUGGEST EFFECTIVE SHEAR VALUES IN EXCESS OF 35 KTS ACROSS NRN IL. GIVEN THIS ENVIRONMENT...THE LINE IS EXPECTED TO CONTINUE PROGRESSING EWD WITH A CONTINUED THREAT OF DAMAGING WINDS AND SEVERE HAIL. CURRENT STORM MOTION IS ESTIMATED AT 250/45 WITH SOME DISCRETE PROPAGATION NOTED ACROSS CEDAR AND JONES COUNTIES. THE LINE WILL LIKELY MOVE OUTSIDE OF WW 557 AND A DOWNSTREAM WW WILL LIKELY BE NEEDED WITHIN THE NEXT HOUR OR TWO. ..MOSIER.. 08/04/2012

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ISOLATED SVR TSTMS PRODUCING DAMAGING DOWNBURST WINDS AND HAIL ARE POSSIBLE THRU THE AFTERNOON HOURS. DUE TO THE LOCALIZED NATURE OF THE SVR THREAT...A WW IS NOT ANTICIPATED AT THIS TIME.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: STG TSTMS CONTINUE TO DEVELOP IN THE VICINITY OF A SURFACE CONFLUENCE ZONE CHARACTERIZED BY STG INSTABILITY /MLCAPE OF 3000-4000 J/KG/...AND MINIMAL CINH. DISCUSSION AREA IS SOUTH OF STRONGER MID-LEVEL FLOW...HOWEVER HIGH VALUES OF PRECIPITABLE WATER /PWATS OF 2 INCHES OR MORE/ AND INCREASING LOW-LEVEL LAPSE RATES EAST OF THE DEVELOPING TSTMS SUGGEST ISOLATED DAMAGING DOWNBURST WINDS WILL BE THE MAIN THREAT. WHERE MERGING OUTFLOWS CAN BECOME ESTABLISHED...CLUSTERS OF SVR TSTMS WITH AN ENHANCED SVR WIND THREAT WILL BE POSSIBLE. A FEW LARGE HAIL REPORTS ARE ALSO NOT OUT OF THE QUESTION GIVEN THE DEGREE OF INSTABILITY.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: LINE OF TSTMS CURRENTLY MOVING ACROSS NRN IL WILL LIKELY REMAIN STRONG AS IT MOVES INTO NRN IND AND SRN LWR MI AND A DOWNSTREAM WW MAY BE NEEDED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LINE OF STG/SVR TSTMS CONTINUES PROGRESSING EWD ACROSS NRN IL. THIS LINE IS BEGINNING TO MOVE AHEAD OF THE BEST SHEAR BUT SHOULD REMAIN ORGANIZED ENOUGH FOR AN INCREASED SVR THREAT ACROSS NRN IND AND SRN LWR MI. DEWPOINT VALUES IN THE MID 70S AND TEMPERATURES IN THE UPPER 80S/LOW 90S ACROSS NRN IND WILL SUPPORT MLCAPE AOA 2500 J/KG WHILE SLIGHTLY LOWER DEWPOINT VALUES WILL SUPPORT MLCAPE NEAR 1500 J/KG FARTHER N. GIVEN THE TIME OF DAY AND ENVIRONMENT DOWNSTREAM OF THE CURRENT MCS...CONTINUED EWD PROGRESSION IS EXPECTED AND A DOWNSTREAM WW MAY BE NEEDED. UNCERTAINTY REGARDING THE PROGRESSION OF THE MCS ACROSS LWR LK MI PRECLUDES HIGHER WATCH PROBABILITIES.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS ARE FORECAST TO DEVELOP THIS EVENING ALONG AND AHEAD OF A COLD FRONT ACROSS PORTIONS OF FAR NERN OK/SERN KS...SRN/CNTRL MO...AND FAR NRN AR. THREAT FOR DAMAGING WINDS AND LARGE HAIL WILL EXIST...TRENDS WILL BE MONITORED FOR A POSSIBLE WW.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: MESOANALYSIS AT 22Z SHOWS A COLD FRONT EXTENDING SWWD FROM CNTRL IL INTO SWRN MO AND NRN OK. TEMPERATURES HAVE WARMED TO NEAR 110F ALONG THE OK PORTION OF THE FRONT...AND HAVE AIDED IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF STEEP LOW-LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND STRONG BOUNDARY LAYER DESTABILIZATION...WHICH HAS FAVORED THE DEVELOPMENT OF A THUNDERSTORM CLUSTER DURING THE LAST HR OR TWO. FARTHER E OVER SRN MO AND FAR NRN AR...VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY SHOWS DEEPENING CUMULUS OCCURRING BETWEEN THE HOTTER/DRIER AIRMASS TO THE W AND SLIGHTLY COOLER/MORE MOIST AIRMASS TO THE E. SHORT-TERM MODEL GUIDANCE INDICATES THIS CUMULUS WILL EVOLVE INTO THUNDERSTORM CLUSTERS...AND THEN SPREAD EWD TOWARD THE MS RIVER DURING THE NIGHT. GIVEN SURFACE CONDITIONS CHARACTERIZED BY TEMPERATURES FROM 90-100F...DEWPOINTS IN THE 60S TO LOW 70S...AND STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES...ESTIMATES OF MLCAPE EXCEED 2000 J/KG OVER THE ERN HALF OF SRN/CNTRL MO. THE LARGE BUOYANCY COMBINED WITH 0-6 KM BULK SHEAR NEAR 30 KT WILL FAVOR STRONG TO SVR MULTICELL THUNDERSTORMS POSING A THREAT FOR DAMAGING WINDS AND LARGE HAIL. MEANWHILE...STORMS OCCURRING OVER FAR NERN OK/SERN KS AND SWRN MO MAY POSE A THREAT FOR ISOLATED DAMAGING WIND GUSTS GIVEN THE PRESENCE OF A HOT AND MORE STRONGLY MIXED BOUNDARY LAYER.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: WW MAY BE CLEARED BEHIND MAIN MCS THAT WAS MOVING EWD 40-45 KT ACROSS SWRN LOWER MI AND NRN INDIANA AS OF 23Z. ADDITIONAL WW AND/OR COUNTY EXTENSIONS OF WW 559 MAY BE REQUIRED E OF PRESENT CONFIGURATION.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: MAIN MCS IS SUPPORTED BY STG LOW-LEVEL COLD POOL WITH 2-4 MB PER 2 HR ISALLOBARS IMMEDIATELY BEHIND MAIN PRECIP AREA...THEN WAKE DEPRESSION OF SIMILAR NEGATIVE MAGNITUDES. THERMODYNAMIC ANALYSES AND MODIFIED FCST SOUNDINGS SUGGEST PATCHY BUT MOSTLY FAVORABLE SUPPORT ACROSS REMAINDER SRN LOWER MI...NERN INDIANA ND NWRN OH. SRN PORTION OF COMPLEX IS OVERTAKING ADDITIONAL/RELATIVELY DISCRETE CONVECTIVE ELEMENTS FORMING IN WARM SECTOR...WHERE 2000-3000 J/KG MLCAPE IS EVIDENT. AS THIS PART OF COMPLEX ENTERS OH...IT WILL MOVE INTO AREAS AT LEAST TEMPORARILY STABILIZED BY SECONDARY TSTM BAND DESCRIBED BELOW. HOWEVER...MOIST/SSWLY-SWLY FLOW FROM SFC TO 850 MB WILL SUPPORT AIR MASS RECOVERY INTO NWRN OH. CORRIDOR OF ENHANCED MIDLEVEL FLOW -- RELATED TO MCV OVER SRN WI -- IS ENHANCING DEEP SHEAR ACROSS NRN INDIANA AND SERN LOWER MI...WITH WSWLY EFFECTIVE SHEAR VECTORS OF 30-40 KT. MIXED SIGNALS LEND UNCERTAINTY TO MAINTENANCE OF THAT PART OF MCS OVER EXTREME NRN INDIANA AND SRN LOWER MI...BUT ANOTHER WW STILL MAY BE NEEDED FARTHER E TOWARD SERN LOWER MI. HIGH THETAE ALSO IS EVIDENT ACROSS SRN LOWER MI...WITH 70S F SFC DEW POINTS AND 1.5-1.75 INCH PW. NRN PORTION OF MCS WILL INTERACT WITH WEAKER/NON-SVR NWRN EXTENSION OF OH CONVECTION BEFORE ENCOUNTERING THAT AIR MASS...THOUGH STRENGTH OF COLD POOL MAY BE MAINTAINED THROUGH RELATIVELY STABLE CORRIDOR JUST E OF MI SEGMENT OF MAIN MCS. SECONDARY BAND OF STG-SVR TSTMS WILL MOVE ENEWD ACROSS PORTIONS NRN ON IN REGIME OF FAVORABLE BUOYANCY AND WEAK CINH FOR A FEW MORE HOURS...BUT MODEST DEEP-LAYER FLOW AND SHEAR. FCST SOUNDINGS SUGGEST 70S F SFC DEW POINTS WILL SUPPRESS RATE OF DIABATIC SFC COOLING AND HELP TO MAINTAIN 1500-3000 J/KG MLCAPE THROUGH AT LEAST 02Z. THEREAFTER...STABILIZATION WILL BE GRADUAL...WHILE LEADING EDGE OF ACTIVIT

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ALTHOUGH SLOW OVERALL WEAKENING TREND MAY BE UNDERWAY...AT LEAST ISOLATED DAMAGING GUST POTENTIAL WILL CONTINUE WITH QLCS CROSSING WRN/NRN OH...NRN PORTION OF WHICH IS MOVING 40-45 KT. CONVECTIVE TRENDS WILL BE MONITORED FOR POSSIBLE WW FARTHER E ACROSS PORTIONS ERN OH AND WRN PA. COUNTY EXTENSION TO EXISTING WW ALSO MAY BE DONE.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: GREATEST SVR POTENTIAL WILL REMAIN DAMAGING WIND...ESPECIALLY WITH THAT PORTION OF THIS COMPLEX N OF ABOUT A PHD-30 N CMH LINE. REFLECTIVITY ANIMATIONS INDICATE EMBEDDED MESOVORTEX...ASSOCIATED WITH BOWING SEGMENT THAT PASSED ACROSS FDY..MAY BE EVOLVING INTO MCV...POTENTIALLY ENHANCING REAR INFLOW PROCESSES. ALTHOUGH MOST CONVECTION-ALLOWING PROGS CONSISTENTLY HAVE WEAKENED THIS COMPLEX WITH EWD EXTENT ACROSS INDIANA/OH...ITS STG COLD POOL AND WELL-DEFINED ISALLOBARIC PERTURBATION INDICATES SOME RISK FOR IT TO REMAIN ORGANIZED ACROSS MOST OF CENTRAL/NRN OH...AS IT MOVES INTO FAVORABLY MOIST AIR MASS. ONLY SLOW DIABATIC SFC COOLING IS EXPECTED...INDICATING THAT FORCED ASCENT OF FAVORABLY MOIST NEAR-SFC INFLOW PARCELS WILL CONTINUE TO SUSTAIN THIS COMPLEX. MLCAPE WILL DECREASE WITH EWD EXTENT ACROSS NRN OH...FROM AROUND 2000 J/KG IN ITS CURRENT PROXIMAL INFLOW TO AROUND 1000 J/KG NEAR PA BORDER WHERE LAPSE RATES ALOFT WILL REMAIN WEAKER. MAIN UNCERTAINTY...GIVEN THESE MIXED SIGNALS...IS HOW LONG COMPLEX CAN SUSTAIN NEAR-SVR LEVEL OF INTENSITY BEFORE SUBSTANTIAL WEAKENING. SEVERAL ESTIMATED SVR GUSTS AND REPORTS OF WIND DAMAGE HAVE BEEN RECEIVED OVER NWRN OH. HOWEVER...MEASURED GUSTS AT STATIONS ACROSS WHICH THIS COMPLEX HAS PASSED HAVE BEEN SUB-SVR...GREATEST BEING 41 KT AT FDY IN BOW APEX. PRIND SVR THREAT WILL BE VERY LOCALIZED...WITH APEX POINTS AND EMBEDDED VORTICES OFFERING GREATEST RISK OF DAMAGING AND PERHAPS SVR GUSTS. ..EDWARDS.. 08/05/2012

mesoscale_discussions.summary: CLUSTER OF STORMS MAY BECOME CAPABLE OF PRODUCING ISOLATED STRONG TO DAMAGING WIND GUSTS AS IT CONTINUES THROUGH CNTRL IND AND EVENTUALLY WRN OH EARLY THIS MORNING. IF STORMS BEGIN TO SHOW SIGNS OF FURTHER INTENSIFICATION AND ORGANIZATION...A WW MIGHT BE REQUIRED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: CLUSTER OF STORMS OVER WCNTRL IND APPEARS TO HAVE INITIATED IN ASSOCIATION WITH INCREASING FRONTOGENETIC FORCING WITHIN BASE OF AMPLIFYING UPPER TROUGH. TRENDS IN LIGHTNING...CLOUD TOPS AND CAPPI INDICATE ACTIVITY HAS INCREASED IN INTENSITY DURING THE PAST HOUR AND IS ALSO BECOMING BETTER ORGANIZED AS A LINE. STORMS APPEAR TO HAVE TRANSITIONED TO A FORWARD PROPAGATING MCS...AND CONCERN IS THAT THEY MAY EVENTUALLY BECOME CAPABLE OF PRODUCING ISOLATED STRONG TO DAMAGING WIND GUSTS. ACTIVITY IS EMBEDDED WITHIN 40-45 KT WSWLY LLJ WHICH MIGHT ENHANCE THE FORMATION OF A REAR INFLOW JET AND AUGMENT THE POTENTIAL FOR DAMAGING WIND...ESPECIALLY GIVEN THE N-S CONVECTIVE LINE ORIENTATION.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THOUGH AN ISOLATED STRONG WIND GUST OR TWO REMAINS POSSIBLE OVER WRN OH NEXT HOUR...OVERALL SEVERE THREAT IS BECOMING INCREASINGLY MARGINAL AND STORMS WILL BEGIN MOVING EAST OF WW 562 BY 13Z. ANOTHER WW IS NOT EXPECTED AT THIS TIME.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: STORMS CONTINUE MOVING THROUGH WRN OH AT 35-40 KT AND RETAIN SOME ORGANIZATIONAL STRUCTURE INCLUDING COMMA HEAD WITH TRAILING LINE SEGMENTS. HOWEVER...INTENSITIES HAVE DECREASED SIGNIFICANTLY...MOST LIKELY DUE TO MARGINAL INSTABILITY. THE INCOMING VISIBLE IMAGERY SHOWS WIDESPREAD CLOUDS AND ELEVATED STORMS DEVELOPING ALONG WARM CONVEYOR BELT AND WITHIN SUBTROPICAL MOISTURE PLUME WHICH SHOULD LIMIT DOWNSTREAM DESTABILIZATION AND REINTENSIFICATION POTENTIAL NEXT FEW HOURS.
